answer: When one operator coordinates k identities to equivocate, the protocol aggregates pairwise evidence and penalizes bonded collateral in proportion to k(k−1)/2, yielding O(k²) loss rather than a separate linear cost per signer. Detection can apply an exponential multiplier to capital loss, compounded by asymmetric depreciation, so splitting control among identities named nebula, umber, or pulse does not evade the risk.
